# Multi Digital: Development & Security Rules

<!-- Managed in the central dev-standard repository and synced here by pull request. Do not edit this file in a project repository. Standard version 1.1, 2026-11-10. -->

These rules bind every developer and every AI agent working in this repository. They are the short form of the Multi Digital Development & Security Standard. The full standard is `docs/DEV-STANDARD.md` (Hebrew). If the two disagree, the full standard wins.

## Before you start

1. Read `docs/PROJECT-NOTES.md` if it exists: the stack, commands, risk level and architecture of this project.
2. Read `EXCEPTIONS.md` if it exists: the approved exceptions to these rules. Nothing else is an exception.
3. Before work on security, privacy, payments, accessibility or deployment, open the matching chapter of `docs/DEV-STANDARD.md` (index at the end of this file).
4. If a request conflicts with a rule, say so and propose a compliant way. Never break a rule silently.

## Rules

The solution must be secure, simple, fast, accessible and tested.

- **Security.** Validate all input server-side against an allowlist. Encode all output for its context. Parameterized queries only. Check authentication, authorization and record ownership on every endpoint. CSRF protection and rate limiting. No secrets in code, logs or the client. No eval, no shell execution, no deserialization of input, no obfuscated code. Argon2id or bcrypt for passwords. TLS everywhere and security headers. Signed webhooks. Generic errors to users, details in server logs only. Minimal, locked and scanned dependencies.
- **Privacy.** Collect the minimum, record consent, define retention, no real personal data in test environments, never store card data.
- **Code.** Official language standard, explicit types, zero warnings, no deprecated APIs, short functions, clear English names, logic separated from presentation, no dead or debug code, explicit error handling, documentation for every significant component.
- **Tests.** Unit and integration tests for all logic, negative authorization tests, a regression test for every bug, all running in CI.
- **Accessibility.** WCAG 2.2 AA and Israeli Standard 5568. Semantic HTML, full keyboard support, visible focus, 4.5:1 contrast, a label for every field, alt text for every image, ARIA only when needed, RTL/LTR and screen-reader support, prefers-reduced-motion respected.
- **Performance.** LCP <= 2.5s, INP <= 200ms, CLS <= 0.1, PageSpeed 90+ on mobile and 95+ on desktop. Load assets only where needed, no N+1 queries, cache everything that is not real-time, heavy work in the background, compatible with CDN and full-page cache.
- **Process.** Git, small pull requests, code review, CI with lint, tests, SAST, dependency scanning and secret scanning. Staging before production. Backup and rollback plan.

## Stack add-ons

Apply every add-on that matches this repository.

- **WordPress.** WordPress Coding Standards, PHP 8.3+. `sanitize_*` on input, `esc_*` on output. Nonce and `current_user_can()` on every action; `permission_callback` on every REST route. `$wpdb->prepare()` for every query. Conditional asset loading per page. Transients and object cache. Compatible with LiteSpeed Cache, Cloudflare, Redis, Memcached, Object Cache Pro and WP Rocket, and with current WooCommerce, Elementor, JetEngine and JetFormBuilder. Also: dedicated admin dashboard, mini CRM for leads, Cloudflare Turnstile on the site and forms, Multi Digital footer credit linking to https://m-d.co.il, and a first-visit privacy notice.
- **Laravel.** Supported Laravel version, PHP 8.3+. `APP_DEBUG` off in production; `env()` only in config files. A Form Request for every input, and only `validated()` data downstream. Explicit `$fillable` on every model. A Policy and an authorization check on every action; tenant isolation through a global scope. Blade output with `{{ }}` only. Eloquent or Query Builder with bindings; an allowlist for column and sort names. Slow work and integrations in queued, retry-safe jobs. Signature-verified webhooks. Money as integers. Pint, Larastan and `composer audit` in CI. A feature test for every route, including negative authorization and cross-tenant tests.
- **JavaScript / TypeScript.** TypeScript strict, no `any`. Runtime schema validation for all external data, including environment variables. Type-aware ESLint and Prettier, zero warnings. No `eval`, no `innerHTML`, no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` without DOMPurify. No secrets in the client bundle: `VITE_` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_` variables are public. Tokens in HttpOnly cookies, never in `localStorage`. Authorization is enforced on the server only; every Server Action and Route Handler checks identity, permission and input. Node.js LTS, install from the lockfile only, a 7-day cooldown for new releases, install scripts off. Vitest, Testing Library and Playwright, including axe. Bundle budget and Core Web Vitals enforced in CI.

## When you finish

Report what was verified, what was not, and which rules were not applied and why. Never claim something was tested if it was not run.
